title: Elegant spiral hides a hungry monster
caption: The barred spiral galaxy NGC 4639, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 4639 · constellation Virgo · about 70 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A bar runs clearly through the bright, round core of NGC 4639 in this Hubble image, and the spiral arms are sprinkled with bright patches of star formation. The galaxy lies over 70 million light-years away in Virgo and is one of about 1500 galaxies in the Virgo Cluster.

Around two thirds of all spirals have a bar, and astronomers suspect they are a normal stage that spirals pass through as they develop. The bright patches in the arms look tiny, but each is several hundred light-years across and holds hundreds or thousands of newborn stars.

The core hides a massive black hole that is swallowing gas around it. This makes the center an active galactic nucleus, or AGN, revealed by telltale features in the galaxy's light and by X-rays from hot gas falling inward. NGC 4639 is a very weak AGN, showing that such activity ranges widely, from quiet galaxies like this one to distant quasars.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.40 x 2.51 arcminutes) and distance (70 million light years), the frame spans roughly 49,000 × 51,000 light-years. Its light set out about 70 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 and combines ultraviolet, visible and near-infrared filters. The color assigned to each filter is not published.
understand.eye: Ultraviolet and infrared light are invisible to the eye, and the galaxy is far too faint to see in this detail without Hubble.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Most galaxies are thought to have a black hole at their center. In quasars, the AGN's emission almost completely outshines the galaxy that hosts it. NGC 4639 sits at the quiet end of that range.
alt: A barred spiral galaxy with a bright round core, a bar through the center and arms sprinkled with bright star-forming patches.
